sections.heading: Menjalankan simulasi
sections.bodyMd: Ikuti **sections** dan **timing** seperti ujian sungguhan. Jangan berhenti di tengah, dan kerjakan dalam satu sesi agar **endurance** kamu terlatih.

sections.heading: Menghadapi tekanan
sections.bodyMd: **Pressure** wajar muncul saat jam berjalan. Latih diri dengan ruang tenang, lalu bangun **stamina** lewat beberapa simulasi penuh.

sections.heading: Membaca hasil
sections.bodyMd: Gunakan **feedback** dari setiap jawaban yang salah. Catat apakah kesalahan itu karena **accuracy** yang kurang atau karena waktu yang tidak cukup.

sections.heading: Menyesuaikan target
sections.bodyMd: Gunakan **calibration** untuk membandingkan perasaanmu dengan hasil **mock** dan **band** yang kamu dapat. Dari sana, tentukan latihan berikutnya.

block3.title: Mengapa Simulasi Penuh Penting
block3.text:
Taking a full mock test is one of the most useful ways to prepare for an English exam. A mock test is a practice exam that follows the same format as the real one. It shows your current level, which is often called your band in official score reports. The goal is not only to get a high score, but also to learn how your performance changes under real conditions.

The test is divided into sections, and each section has its own timing. Many candidates feel confident at the start, but they lose accuracy when time becomes short. A good practice habit is to set a timer for each section and to stop when the time ends, even if the last question is unfinished. This builds the discipline that the real exam requires.

Pressure is another part of the experience. Some students become nervous when they hear a clock or see a long text. Practising in a quiet room with no phone nearby helps the mind become used to this feeling. Over time, pressure becomes less surprising, and the brain can focus on the task rather than on fear.

Endurance matters because the reading and listening papers together take a long time. Concentration can drop after an hour, which is why a short break is not a sign of weakness. Stamina is the ability to keep working well until the last minute. Candidates build stamina through several full practice sessions, not only through short exercises.

After each mock test, the most valuable step is feedback. Look at every wrong answer and ask why it happened. Was the question misread, was a keyword missed, or was the time too short? Writing down these reasons helps you find patterns. Many learners discover that they lose more marks from careless errors than from lack of knowledge.

Calibration is the process of checking whether your self-assessment matches your real results. Some learners think they are at band six, but their mock scores show band five. Calibration helps them adjust their expectations and choose the right study plan. It is better to know the truth early than to be surprised on exam day.

A useful schedule might include one full mock test each week during the final month. Between tests, focus on the sections where your accuracy is lowest. For example, if true, false, and not given questions cause problems, practise only that question type for twenty minutes each day. Then return to a full test to check whether the improvement lasts under pressure.

Finally, remember that a mock test is a tool, not a judgement of your value. A low score in one practice session does not mean you cannot succeed. It means you have useful information about what to study next. Used carefully, each mock test turns uncertainty into a clear plan.
